title: Hybrid quantum-classical architecture: orchestrator, job queue and backend adapter
description: Design the loop around a variational algorithm: an orchestrator with a job queue policy, a transpile cache and retries, behind a backend adapter; compare sync, batched and session execution on a fake clock.
outcome: You can separate optimiser, orchestrator and backend; choose an execution mode from measured wall time, billed time and job counts; key a transpile cache correctly; make retries idempotent; and keep the decision true with a fitness test.
environment: Mac mini or Windows 11; Python 3.12 venv (lesson 1); numpy 2.5.3 (+ cryptography 50.0.2 for lesson 21) from labs/L400/requirements.txt; shared numpy simulators in labs/_shared (qsim, qopt). SDK path: qiskit 2.6.1 StatevectorSampler with a PUB parameter array per step + generate_preset_pass_manager on GenericBackendV2 (sampler_qiskit.py) (pending CI).
overview: The circuit is the easy part: on shared devices the queue, the compiler and failed jobs decide how long a variational run takes and what it costs.
prerequisites: distributed-systems L100 #4 retries and L300 #16 backpressure (helpful, not required)

glossary.meaning: Code between optimiser and backend that owns batching, caching and retries.
A small interface (transpile, run, open/close session) that hides a simulator or provider.
One submission that carries every circuit of one optimiser step (Qiskit: one PUB with a parameter array).
A reserved device window: later jobs skip the queue, the whole window is billed, an interactive TTL ends it.
Re-running a failed job gives exactly the same result because each circuit carries its seed.
A modelled clock that the code advances; tests stay deterministic and never sleep.

concepts: Execution mode is an architecture decision with measurable cost.
Cache compiled circuits by structure and target, never by angle.
Retries must not change the answer.
Fitness tests keep the decision true as code changes.

designBrief.context: A multi-start SPSA QAOA loop (4 starts x 30 iterations = 240 circuits of one template) must run on a shared backend with a 2 s queue per job, 0.5 s per transpile and occasional transient job failures.
constraints: modelled wall time <= 90 s for the reference workload
billed device time <= 5 s
<= 1 job per optimiser step
exactly 1 transpile per template and target
a transient failure must not change the result
designBrief.question: Which execution mode (sync loop, batched jobs, session) and which cache/retry policy should the service use by default?

options.name: Synchronous loop (one job per circuit)
options.description: Submit each circuit as soon as the optimiser asks for it.
options.evidence: 486.8 s modelled wall, 4.8 s billed, 240 jobs (with the structural cache); 7206.8 s with a 30 s queue.

options.name: Batched jobs (one job per optimiser step)
options.description: Submit all circuits of an SPSA step together; structural transpile cache; idempotent retries.
options.evidence: 66.8 s wall, 4.8 s billed, 30 jobs, 1 transpile; 3 seeded failures add 10.0 s and leave best_ratio 0.6922 unchanged.

options.name: Session + batches
options.description: Reserve the device; jobs after the first skip the queue; billed for the window.
options.evidence: 11.7 s wall but 11.7 s billed (2.4x); with a 70 s classical step the TTL expires and billing reaches 2165.3 s for the same wall time as batched.

fitnessFunction.what: The default mode stays 'batched'; one job per optimiser step; one transpile per template; wall and billing within budget.
fitnessFunction.threshold: jobs <= 30, transpiles == 1, modelled wall <= 90 s, billed <= 5 s for the reference workload

scalingLimits: Queue-dominated wall time: when jobs x queue >> execution (signal: wall_s >> billed_s), batch more per job or consider sessions.
Provider batch limits (max_circuits): the adapter raises ValueError; chunking adds one queue wait per chunk.
Adaptive ansaetze create new templates each step: cache hit rate falls below ~0.99 and transpile time returns.

title: Benchmarking honestly against classical solvers
description: Compare QAOA with exact, greedy and simulated-annealing MaxCut solvers at sizes the simulator handles; fix a biased comparison method and guard it with a fitness test.
outcome: You can design a fair benchmark (same budget, same seeds, medians, enforced budgets), compute quality and time-to-solution, let code pick the winner, and explain when quantum is not the right tool.

code:
"""Lab 18 - benchmarking QAOA honestly against classical MaxCut solvers (simulator only).

Run:  python bench_lab.py          (numpy only; JSON lines)   Fair version: python solution_fair.py
Solvers (solvers.py): exact brute force (the reference), greedy local search, simulated annealing, QAOA p=1.
Quality = approximation ratio (best cut / exact optimum). Time-to-solution = samples until the best cut was
first seen, and TTS99 = budget x ln(0.01)/ln(1 - success rate). Local seconds are printed but never judged:
simulator time says nothing about hardware time.
The FAULT is this file's compare(): QAOA gets 4x the budget and its best of 10 seeds, the classical baselines
run once at a quarter budget, and nobody checks what a solver spent - the classic way a benchmark "shows" a quantum win.
SDK path (QAOA sampled with Qiskit StatevectorSampler): python bench_qiskit.py   (CI)
"""
import json
import math
import time

import numpy as np

import solvers as S

SIZES, SEEDS, BUDGET = (8, 12, 16), tuple(range(10)), 200
CLASSICAL = ("greedy", "annealing")


def instance(n, seed=0):
    edges = S.mc.regular_graph(n, 3, seed=100 + seed)
    return edges, S.exact(n, edges)["cut"]


def tts99(success_rate, samples_per_run):
    """Samples for 99 % confidence of seeing the optimum at least once (repeat-until-success)."""
    if success_rate == 0:
        return None                     # never found: no finite time-to-solution
    if success_rate == 1:
        return samples_per_run
    return round(samples_per_run * math.log(0.01) / math.log(1 - success_rate))


def summarise(n, name, results, opt, budget, seconds):
    ratios = [r["cut"] / opt for r in results]
    rate = float(np.mean([r["cut"] == opt for r in results]))
    return {"n": n, "solver": name, "budget": budget, "runs": len(results),
            "median_ratio": round(float(np.median(ratios)), 4), "success": rate,
            "median_first_best": int(np.median([r["first_best"] for r in results])),
            "tts99_samples": tts99(rate, budget), "local_s": round(seconds, 3)}


def decide(rows):
    """Code decides the winner: quality, then reliability, then speed; a tie goes to the classical baseline."""
    key = lambda r: (r["median_ratio"], r["success"], -r["median_first_best"], r["solver"] in CLASSICAL)  # noqa: E731
    return max(rows, key=key)["solver"]


BOOST = {"qaoa": 4, "greedy": 0.25, "annealing": 0.25}   # FAULT 1: QAOA tuned with 4x shots, baselines left at 50


def compare(n, solvers=S.BUDGETED, budget=BUDGET, seeds=SEEDS):
    edges, opt = instance(n)
    rows = []
    for name, solve in solvers.items():
        t = time.perf_counter()
        runs = seeds if name not in CLASSICAL else seeds[:1]     # FAULT 2: the baseline is run once
        results = [solve(n, edges, int(budget * BOOST.get(name, 1)), s) for s in runs]
        best = max(results, key=lambda r: r["cut"])              # FAULT 3: best seed reported as "the" result
        rows.append(summarise(n, name, [best], opt, budget, (time.perf_counter() - t) / len(runs)))
    return rows, decide(rows)                                    # FAULT 4: nobody checks r["used"] <= budget


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for n in SIZES:
        rows, winner = compare(n)
        for r in rows:
            print(json.dumps(r))
        print(json.dumps({"n": n, "winner": winner, "method": "naive (unequal budget, best seed)"}))

code:
"""Lab 19 - resource estimation: from problem size to logical and physical qubits, depth, CX and T counts.

Run:  python estimate_lab.py     (numpy/stdlib only; prints JSON lines)
1. Logical counts for QAOA MaxCut on 3-regular graphs (formulas, validated against counted circuits for n <= 12).
2. Shor/RSA logical counts from Gidney & Ekera (2021, arXiv:1905.09749) abstract formulas.
3. Surface-code overhead: p_L(d) = 0.03 (p / 0.01)^((d+1)/2) per logical qubit per logical cycle (Fowler et al.
   2012 Eq. 11; the defaults of qdk.qre's SurfaceCode), about 2 d^2 physical qubits per logical qubit
   (d^2 data + d^2 - 1 measure). Data blocks only: no magic-state factories, no routing -> a LOWER bound.
4. A feasibility class per workload. The FAULT: choose_distance() below uses a fixed d = 3 ("17 physical per logical").
QDK path (qdk.qre estimator on the same QAOA program): python estimate_qdk.py   (CI job l400-qdk)
"""
import json
import math

from counting import t_per_rotation

P_PHYS, CYCLE_S, BUDGET = 1e-3, 1e-6, 0.01        # gate error, surface-code cycle (1 us), total failure budget
THRESHOLDS = {"sim_qubits": 30, "nisq_esp": 0.5, "max_physical": 1_000_000, "max_runtime_s": 86_400}


def qaoa_logical(n, p, colours=4, eps_total=1e-3):
    edges = 3 * n // 2
    rotations = p * (edges + n)
    t_rot = t_per_rotation(eps_total / rotations)                   # synthesis error shared by all rotations
    depth = 1 + p * (3 * colours + 1)                                # colour groups of RZZ run in parallel
    return {"workload": f"qaoa n={n} p={p}", "logical_qubits": n, "cx": 2 * edges * p, "rotations": rotations,
            "depth": depth, "t_count": rotations * t_rot,
            "logical_cycles": depth + p * (colours + 1) * t_rot}       # each rotation layer = t_rot T steps


def rsa_logical(bits):
    lg = math.log2(bits)
    toffoli = 0.3 * bits ** 3 + 0.0005 * bits ** 3 * lg
    out = {"workload": f"rsa-{bits}", "logical_qubits": math.ceil(3 * bits + 0.002 * bits * lg),
            "toffoli": round(toffoli), "t_count": 7 * round(toffoli),      # 7 T per Toffoli (counting.toffoli_ok)
            "depth": round(500 * bits ** 2 + bits ** 2 * lg)}              # measurement depth
    out["logical_cycles"] = out["depth"]
    return out


def logical_error(d, p=P_PHYS, a=0.03, p_th=0.01):
    return a * (p / p_th) ** ((d + 1) / 2)


def choose_distance(p, logical_qubits, cycles, budget=BUDGET):
    """NAIVE: one fixed code distance for every workload ('a logical qubit is 17 physical qubits')."""
    return 3


def physical(est, p=P_PHYS, choose=choose_distance):
    cycles = est["logical_cycles"]
    d = choose(p, est["logical_qubits"], cycles)
    fail = min(1.0, est["logical_qubits"] * cycles * logical_error(d, p))
    return {**est, "distance": d, "physical_qubits": est["logical_qubits"] * 2 * d * d,
            "runtime_s": float(f"{cycles * d * CYCLE_S:.4g}"), "p_fail": float(f"{fail:.3g}")}


def classify(est):
    """Code decides: run where the estimate says it can run."""
    esp = (1 - P_PHYS) ** est.get("cx", math.inf)
    if est["logical_qubits"] <= THRESHOLDS["sim_qubits"]:
        return "simulate"
    if esp >= THRESHOLDS["nisq_esp"]:
        return "nisq-candidate"
    if est["physical_qubits"] <= THRESHOLDS["max_physical"] and est["runtime_s"] <= THRESHOLDS["max_runtime_s"]:
        return "fault-tolerant-feasible"
    return "infeasible (assumptions above)"


WORKLOADS = [qaoa_logical(20, 1), qaoa_logical(100, 1), qaoa_logical(100, 4), qaoa_logical(1000, 10),
             rsa_logical(1024), rsa_logical(2048)]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for est in WORKLOADS:
        row = physical(est)
        print(json.dumps({**row, "class": classify(row)}))

codeWalkthrough.detail: Builds the QAOA circuit as explicit ops (RZZ = CX RZ CX, edges grouped by colour) and counts CX, rotations and ASAP depth - the ground truth for small n.

codeWalkthrough.detail: Checks the textbook 7-T Toffoli decomposition against the exact Toffoli unitary: the 7 T per Toffoli used for Shor is verified, not assumed.

codeWalkthrough.title: qaoa_logical
codeWalkthrough.detail: Formulas that scale to any n: CX = 2|E|p, rotations = p(|E| + n), depth = 1 + p(3c + 1), T = rotations x 3 log2(1/eps) (Ross-Selinger), logical cycles include T-limited rotation layers.

codeWalkthrough.title: rsa_logical
codeWalkthrough.detail: Gidney & Ekera's abstract formulas: 3n + 0.002 n lg n logical qubits, 0.3n^3 + 0.0005 n^3 lg n Toffolis, 500n^2 + n^2 lg n measurement depth.

codeWalkthrough.title: logical_error / physical
codeWalkthrough.detail: p_L(d) = 0.03 (p/0.01)^((d+1)/2) (Fowler Eq. 11, QDK SurfaceCode defaults); physical = logical x 2d^2; runtime = cycles x d x 1 us; p_fail = qubits x cycles x p_L.

codeWalkthrough.title: choose_distance (the fault)
codeWalkthrough.detail: Shipped: always 3. The build task chooses the smallest odd d that meets the 1 % budget and refuses at or above the threshold.

codeWalkthrough.title: classify
codeWalkthrough.detail: Policy: simulate (<= 30 qubits), NISQ candidate ((1-1e-3)^CX >= 0.5), fault-tolerant-feasible (<= 1e6 physical, <= 1 day), else infeasible.

code:
"""Lab 21 - quantum and post-quantum: inventory a codebase's crypto and plan the migration.

Run:  python pqc_lab.py      (stdlib + cryptography 50.0.2; ML-KEM-768 runs locally)
1. Shor in context: what breaking RSA-2048 / P-256 needs (lesson 19's model + published estimates).
2. Inventory toy_app/: every public-key use, its purpose, and the data's secrecy lifetime.
3. Plan: replacement per NIST IR 8547 (ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA for signatures, keep AES-256),
   priority by Mosca's inequality X + Y > Z ("harvest now, decrypt later").
4. Crypto agility: X25519 vs ML-KEM-768 vs the hybrid, behind one interface (agility.py).
The FAULT: scan() below is a grep for "RSA". Fix it in the build task (solution_scanner.py).
"""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import agility
import shor_context

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
APP = HERE / "toy_app"
MIGRATION_YEARS, YEARS_TO_CRQC = 3, 9          # Y and Z in Mosca's inequality: planning assumptions, not forecasts
REPLACEMENT = {"key-establishment": "ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203); hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 during transition",
               "signature": "ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204)", "symmetric": "keep (AES-256 / SHA-256 not broken by Shor)"}


def scan(root=APP):
    """NAIVE: grep every file for 'rsa'. Finds words, not uses: misses X25519/ECDH/ECDSA, flags a docstring."""
    found = []
    for path in sorted(p for p in root.rglob("*") if p.suffix in (".py", ".toml")):
        for no, text in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
            m = re.search(r"rsa[-_]?(\d+)?", text, re.I)
            if m:
                found.append({"file": path.relative_to(HERE).as_posix(), "line": no,
                              "algorithm": f"RSA-{m.group(1)}" if m.group(1) else "RSA", "usage": "unknown"})
    return found


def plan(inventory, classification=None):
    """Code decides priority: P1 if key establishment protects data that must outlive Z - Y years (HNDL)."""
    classification = classification or json.loads((APP / "data_classification.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    steps = []
    for item in inventory:
        years = classification.get(item["file"], {}).get("secrecy_years", 0)
        if item["usage"] == "key-establishment" and years + MIGRATION_YEARS > YEARS_TO_CRQC:
            prio = "P1 now (harvest now, decrypt later)"
        elif item["usage"] in ("key-establishment", "signature", "unknown"):
            prio = "P2 before 2030 (deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035)"
        else:
            prio = "none"
        steps.append({**item, "secrecy_years": years, "priority": prio,
                      "replacement": REPLACEMENT.get(item["usage"], "review manually")})
    return sorted(steps, key=lambda s: (s["priority"], s["file"], s["line"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps({"shor_model": shor_context.our_model(), "ecc": shor_context.ecc_logical(256)}))
    for cited in shor_context.CITED:
        print(json.dumps(cited))
    inventory = scan()
    print(json.dumps({"scanner": "grep", "findings": len(inventory)}))
    for step in plan(inventory):
        print(json.dumps(step))
    for name in agility.REGISTRY:
        print(json.dumps(agility.measure(name)))

title: Capstone: an end-to-end quantum optimisation service
description: An HTTP service that gates each MaxCut request on a resource estimate, runs noisy QAOA through the lesson 17 orchestrator on a compiled fake device, mitigates readout error, benchmarks it fairly against classical solvers, lets code pick the winner and has a local model explain the report.
outcome: You can assemble the topic's labs into one service with explicit decisions (four ADRs), prove each milestone with tests, and print a scorecard where code - not the agent - decides which solver wins under the budget.
environment: Mac mini or Windows 11; Python 3.12 venv (lesson 1); numpy 2.5.3 (+ cryptography 50.0.2 for lesson 21) from labs/L400/requirements.txt; shared numpy simulators in labs/_shared (qsim, qopt). SDK path: optional: swap NoisyBackend for a Qiskit Aer adapter and the mitigation for Mitiq REM (not built; see KNOWN-GAPS) (pending CI).
overview: One request, every lesson: feasibility gate (19), orchestrated noisy QAOA (17, 12, 20), mitigation (13), fair benchmark (18), code decides, agent explains.
prerequisites: L100 #5 agent assist pattern (model proposes, code decides)

designBrief.context: Clients post MaxCut instances (4-16 nodes) and want the best cut and an honest answer to 'should we use the quantum solver?'. The only device is a fake 8-qubit ladder with a drifted coupler; backend jobs fail transiently.
constraints: every solver gets the same sample budget and seeds
a request the device cannot hold never reaches the quantum path
modelled wall time per request <= 60 s, one transpile per request
transient job failures do not change results
the agent only explains; code decides; nothing binds beyond 127.0.0.1
designBrief.question: What does the service run for each request, and who decides which solver's answer wins?

architecture.summary: service.py validates POST /solve and calls pipeline.solve: a lesson-19 feasibility gate decides whether a quantum path exists; if so, lesson 17's Orchestrator (batched jobs, structural cache, retries) drives SPSA-trained QAOA on a NoisyBackend adapter that compiles with lesson 20's router (ESP, depth budget) and samples a white-noise + readout model checked against a density-matrix simulation; lesson 13's constrained mitigation corrects the readout bias of <C>; lesson 18's fair harness runs greedy, annealing and QAOA at the same budget and seeds and decide() picks the winner; agent_assist.py asks a local model to explain the report and code rejects explanations whose winner, numbers or claims disagree.

code:
"""Capstone runner: drive the service end to end and print a scorecard as JSON lines.

Run: python run_capstone.py      (numpy + stdlib; the agent uses the deterministic fake model server)
Seeded faults: transient backend failures on job attempts 3 and 4, and the drifted CX edge (1, 2) on the device.
Every milestone and rubric line is decided by code; the agent's explanation is only checked, never trusted.
"""
import functools
import json
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import agent_assist
import fake_explain_rule
import noisy_backend as nb
import pipeline
import service
from reuse import l18_bench

IGNORE = ("local_s",)


def call(url, path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url + path, data=None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        with e:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read())


def rows(report):
    return [{k: v for k, v in r.items() if k not in IGNORE} for r in report["benchmark"]]


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def collect():
    server, url = service.start()
    try:
        out = {"health": call(url, "/health"), "default": call(url, "/solve", {}), "bad": call(url, "/solve", {"n": 30}),
               "large": call(url, "/solve", {"n": 12})}
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
    out["no_faults"] = pipeline.solve({"faults": []})
    out["white_noise"] = nb.white_noise_check()
    from local_agent import fake_model_server
    fake_explain_rule.register(fake_model_server)
    fake, fake_url = fake_model_server.start_in_thread()
    try:
        out["agent"] = agent_assist.run(out["default"][1], fake_url)
    finally:
        fake.shutdown()
    return out


def milestones(o):
    rep, large = o["default"][1], o["large"][1]
    ex, cp, mt = rep["execution"], rep["compile"], rep["mitigation"]
    return [
        ("M1 API and validation", o["health"][0] == 200 and o["default"][0] == 200 and o["bad"][0] == 400 and o["large"][0] == 200,
         {"health": o["health"][0], "solve": o["default"][0], "bad_request": o["bad"][0], "bad_reason": o["bad"][1]["error"]}),
        ("M2 orchestrated quantum path (batched, cached, retried)",
         ex["mode"] == "batched" and ex["transpiles"] == 1 and ex["jobs"] <= 10 and ex["retries"] == 2 and rows(rep) == rows(o["no_faults"]), ex),
        ("M3 compile + noise model", cp["within_depth_budget"] and o["white_noise"]["tvd_model"] <= 0.03 < o["white_noise"]["tvd_ideal"],
         {**{k: cp[k] for k in ("esp", "cx", "depth", "gate_fidelity")}, **o["white_noise"]}),
        ("M4 readout mitigation", abs(mt["mitigated"] - mt["gate_noise_only"]) < abs(mt["raw"] - mt["gate_noise_only"]), mt),
        ("M5 fair benchmark + code decides", len({r["budget"] for r in rep["benchmark"]}) == 1
         and {r["runs"] for r in rep["benchmark"]} == {rep["request"]["seeds"]} and rep["winner"] == l18_bench.decide(rep["benchmark"])
         and not large["feasibility"]["quantum_path"], {"winner": rep["winner"], "n12_winner": large["winner"],
                                                         "n12_reason": large["feasibility"]["reason"]}),
        ("M6 agent explains, code checks", [o["agent"][k][0] for k in ("explain", "pitch", "brief")] == ["ACCEPT", "REJECT", "REJECT"],
         {k: (v[0], v[1]) for k, v in o["agent"].items()}),
    ]


def rubric(o):
    rep = o["default"][1]
    best = next(r for r in rep["benchmark"] if r["solver"] == rep["winner"])
    return [
        ("correctness", f"winner median ratio {best['median_ratio']}", best["median_ratio"] >= 0.95),
        ("fairness", "one budget and one seed list for every solver", len({(r["budget"], r["runs"]) for r in rep["benchmark"]}) == 1),
        ("reliability", "2 injected job failures retried; results identical to a fault-free run", rows(rep) == rows(o["no_faults"])),
        ("cost", f"modelled wall {rep['execution']['wall_s']} s, {rep['execution']['jobs']} jobs (budget 60 s)", rep["execution"]["wall_s"] <= 60),
        ("honesty", "n = 12 refused for the 8-qubit device; classical answer returned", not o["large"][1]["feasibility"]["quantum_path"]),
        ("safety", "agent cannot change the winner; server binds 127.0.0.1", o["agent"]["pitch"][0] == "REJECT"),
    ]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    o = collect()
    ms = milestones(o)
    for name, ok, measure in ms:
        print(json.dumps({"milestone": name, "pass": bool(ok), "measure": measure}))
    rb = rubric(o)
    for criterion, measure, ok in rb:
        print(json.dumps({"rubric": criterion, "measure": measure, "pass": bool(ok)}))
    print(json.dumps({"scorecard": f"{sum(bool(m[1]) for m in ms)}/{len(ms)} milestones, {sum(bool(r[2]) for r in rb)}/{len(rb)} rubric",
                      "winner": o["default"][1]["winner"], "decided_by": "code"}))
